articles.title_zh: Trump now says the Kennedy Center could be deadly. Months ago, it was ‘great.’
articles.content_orig:
Whistleblowers are alleging that Kennedy Center officials halted plans earlier this year to repair leaks in the building, which the Trump administration has highlighted as its reason to close the storied arts institution.
In a letter to Congress Thursday, obtained by CNN, a lawyer representing the anonymous whistleblowers wrote that the Kennedy Center’s director Matt Floca has known about leak issues “for years” and stopped plans for repairs in April, despite receiving $9.3 million dollars in congressional funding for roofing replacement last year.
Repairs “were not treated as priorities nor as acute risks to public safety,” attorney David Seide said in the letter to congressional committees that oversee the arts center. The whistleblowers claimed that Floca requested and received funding for repairs but “stopped the remediation process from moving forward.”
The whistleblowers said Floca received the funds through Trump’s hallmark One Big Beautiful Bill Act but he has delayed addressing the repairs since the bill’s passage last year.
Members of Kennedy Center leadership and President Donald Trump have repeatedly pointed to a September 4 incident where a section of ceiling plaster fell in the Grand Foyer as justification for needing to close their doors. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick shared security video of the piece of ceiling falling, later shared by Trump, as further evidence that the center has “completely unsafe conditions” and declared “people cannot be allowed to go into this building any longer.”
The Kennedy Center in a statement to CNN on Friday pushed back on the whistleblowers’ claims, saying, “The safety of our patrons, artists, and staff comes first.”
“The Kennedy Center has known for years that the roof overhang leaked. What we did not know until this summer was how far the damage had spread inside it,” Floca said in the statement, adding there “was a change in the approach to procuring and delivering the work, not a determination that the work was unnecessary.”
The New York Times was first to report on the whistleblowers’ letter.
The whistleblowers’ claims are the latest development amid a lawsuit brought by Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty, an ex-officio member of the board, to block Trump’s name from being added to the center.
Lawyers for the arts venue have argued that if the current building cannot undergo more extensive renovations, the center “ will deteriorate further into an unsafe, decrepit structure that will be required to be taken down.”
The center said earlier this week in a court filing it will temporarily close until September 30 to assess safety risks.
Trump, who in his second term has installed himself as chairman of the center’s board and overseen sweeping changes to its leadership and programming, announced earlier this year that the center would close for approximately two years for renovations.
It was slated to close on July 4, but a federal judge temporarily blocked the move.
The Trump administration and the Kennedy Center board have continued to push back in the ongoing legal challenge. Lawyers for the center threatened to demolish the building if renovations aren’t allowed.

articles.title_orig: Dante Moore injury: Oregon QB takes scary hit to head, carted off field, put in ambulance
articles.title_zh: Dante Moore injury: Oregon QB takes scary hit to head, carted off field, put in ambulance
articles.content_orig:
Oregon and USC faced off Saturday night, reviving an old Pac-12 rivalry between two powerhouse programs now in the Big Ten. But early in the second quarter, Oregon quarterback Dante Moore went down with one of the scariest injuries of the 2026 season.
Flanked by four Trojans rushers, the Ducks' star QB scrambled out of the pocket and ran up the middle of the field for a big gain. But while trying to slide down at the end of the run, his head slammed into the ground following a late hit from USC's Desman Stephens II. The play drew an immediate targeting flag, and Stephens was ejected from the game.
Moore was tended to on the field for several minutes before being placed on a backboard, carted off, and taken away by ambulance. He was reportedly moving his arms as he left and has since been transported to a local hospital in Los Angeles.
More news : Jon Sumrall Drags His Wife Into Fiery Florida Rant After Ole Miss Blowout
Moore is one of the best quarterbacks and biggest names in college football . He earned third-team All-Big Ten honors last season, his first as Oregon's starter after backing up Dillon Gabriel, throwing for 3,565 yards and 30 touchdowns with 10 interceptions while completing 71.8% of his passes, along with 156 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns. He led the Ducks to a 13-2 record and the College Football Playoff, where they fell in the semifinals to eventual national champion Indiana.
Moore entered this season as one of the favorites for several national awards, including the Walter Camp, Davey O'Brien, and Maxwell Award, and a projected early first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

The hope is that Moore's injury proves less severe than it looked and doesn't keep him out long. If it does, Oregon isn't in bad shape at backup, though, with Dylan Raiola, a former five-star recruit and two-year starter at Nebraska, ready to step in. We should hopefully learn more about the extent of Moore's injury sometime tomorrow.

The controversial Orange Order parade due to go ahead this morning for the first time in nearly 30 years after a late-night ruling is being delayed by protesters.
An 'unprecedented' sitting of the High Court in Belfast upheld a ruling by the Parades Commission permitting the march on Garvaghy Road.
But thousands of protesters gathered in the rain just minutes before the Protestant parade was due to begin in Portadown.
They linked arms and sang songs in an attempt to block the march as an announcement over a loudspeaker told them that they were liable for arrest for taking part in an unnotified parade.
The crowds, many of them wearing balaclavas, clustered in large groups along Garvaghy Road in the hours leading up to the scheduled start of the parade at 8am.
But as of 9am, the march still had not started due to the road being blocked, with members of the Orange Order being asked by police to stay inside Drumcree Church.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appealed for 'calm on all sides', saying there have been 'big gains made in Northern Ireland, and we don't want to see things go backwards'.
Armoured vehicles have arrived and police are operating checkpoints on the main roads into Portadown.
An information sheet is being handed to drivers, reports the BBC , which reads: ' You are entitled to disagree with the procession and to make your views known peacefully.
'The procession has been permitted by a determination of the Parades Commission. People taking part in it also have a right to do so peacefully and safely.'

'I commend this community. We stand with this community and we will continue to stand with this community.'

Some in the crowd blocking the Garvaghy Road on Sunday morning could be heard shouting 'bring Stormont down'.

articles.title_orig: A ‘Big Problem’: Trump’s War With Iran Drags Down Republicans in Midterms
articles.title_zh: A ‘Big Problem’: Trump’s War With Iran Drags Down Republicans in Midterms
articles.content_orig:
At least 17 members of Congress have called on the president to end the war.
Several Republicans running in competitive statewide and federal races are joining growing calls in their party to end the war in Iran with less than 40 days until the midterm elections.
As of Friday, 17 incumbent congressional Republicans running for re-election or non-incumbent candidates for Senate or governor's seats have called for an end to the war, either through votes in Congress to rein in President Donald Trump’s war powers or in statements on the campaign trail or online.
This comes as diesel fuel prices have jumped by nearly 60% since the conflict began at the end of February and as voters sour on the president -- a CNN poll conducted last week found 67% of Americans disapproved of Trump's job performance and 73% disapproved of how he was handling the situation in Iran. And 73% of Americans said that the war with Iran was having a negative effect on their financial situation, including 59% of Republicans.
Since the war in Iran started, Congress has voted on resolutions calling on Trump to get Congress' approval to continue hostilities in Iran. Of the 20 resolutions voted on, some Republicans have voted with Democrats five times to pass resolutions, though they don't force the president to do anything.
The GOP candidates who have broken with Trump on the war include six incumbent members of Congress running for reelection and five Republicans running in statewide races. Four of those five are currently in Congress and have voted against the war powers resolutions.
Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, a former congressman, cut an ad on Monday saying, "The war with Iran needs to end and end quickly. When it does, energy costs will plummet." He has since said that any deal to end the war must ensure Iran can't build a nuclear weapon, Trump's stated goal for the conflict.
In Wisconsin, Rep. Tom Tiffany, the GOP nominee for governor, told ABC affiliate WISN on Wednesday, "it's time to move on."
"The president has final say in regards to this, but I just believe that we should be exiting Iran -- that it's time to move on," Tiffany said. "We've degraded their nuclear facilities. We degraded their military. Most of their ships are in the bottom of the ocean. Time to come home, take care of business here in America."
Tiffany's opponent, Democrat Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, put out an ad this week that slammed the congressman for voting in lockstep with the president on the war.
"Five times he has had the chance to end the war that’s driving our prices up, and five times he’s chosen Trump instead. Tom Tiffany’s only loyal to Trump -- not us, Wisconsin,” Crowley said in a press release.
Ohio Republican Sen. John Husted, facing a tight race for reelection, told Politico on Tuesday, "The war needs to come to an end as quickly as possible so that we can lower gas prices," but he again voted against a war powers resolution on Thursday.
Iowa Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson, who's running in a tight Senate race, has voted against war powers resolutions, but reversed her position on Monday, calling for an "immediate end" to the war.
"Iowans are being squeezed and shouldn’t have to foot the bill at the pump or the checkout line for the war in Iran," she wrote. "We need to use every option at our disposal to provide some relief from high prices. … These actions to lower costs are needed ASAP, and the war needs to be brought to a successful and immediate end.”
A day later, she insisted the House return to Washington, D.C. to address rising fuel prices, promising to "work with anyone to deliver."
“The House should return to DC immediately to work to pause diesel exports, suspend the gas tax, fully unleash E15 and biodiesel, and work on a diesel relief program for truckers and farmers," Hinson wrote on X .
House Speaker Mike Johnson last week canceled the two remaining weeks of its session and let the House leave early, saying, "It's time for our members to go home to their districts and make their case to the American people to go and explain all the great things we've done."
Hinson's Democratic opponent Josh Turek, a state lawmaker, responded on X , "It's easy to send a tweet but when you had the chance to vote to end this war, you chose not to. You voted seven times to continue it, including just last week."
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries criticized the Republicans who have recently broken with Trump on the war during a news conference Wednesday, saying that several of them are "on the verge of losing."
"Where were these Republican sycophants over the last six-plus months?" he said.
Iowa Republican Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks, who had opposed the war powers resolution but voted in favor of it last week, said in a statement, "Americans do not want another forever war."
She cited her military service and acknowledged the rising gas prices driven by the war in Iran, saying that Iowans are "paying too much at the pump."
And Iowa Republican Rep. Zach Nunn voted against previous war powers resolutions but broke with the president on the most recent vote.
"Iowa has already paid a devastating price, including two service members killed by an Iranian drone in Kuwait."
Nunn also recently demanded action on diesel prices, writing on X on Monday , "My plan: Sell American energy to Americans first. Pass my Iowa-led biofuel bill = bring down gas 50 cents. Hold Big Oil accountable for gouging," Nunn wrote.
ABC News' Lalee Ibssa, Jonathan Parker, Laura Peller and John Parkinson contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Anger grows across Spain after elderly woman evicted from her home of 70 years
articles.title_zh: Anger grows across Spain after elderly woman evicted from her home of 70 years
articles.content_orig:
An 87-year-old Spanish woman was forcibly evicted Wednesday from the Madrid apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years, in a case that highlights a growing housing crisis in the country.
Video showed Maricarmen Abascal, who is a wheelchair user, being taken out of the building in the Spanish capital’s Retiro neighborhood on a stretcher and driven away in an ambulance.
Supporters had gathered outside her building overnight on Friday, with dozens of police officers holding them back as some tried to stop the eviction from going ahead. In a social media video posted Friday by the Madrid tenants union, Abascal gave thanks for the support she had received.
Abascal’s lawyer, Beatriz Duro, described the force used in the eviction as “completely disproportionate and unnecessary” and decried the intransigence of the building’s owners.
The case has brought new attention to an ongoing housing crisis in major cities across Spain, as gentrification has caused rents to skyrocket and the stock of affordable housing to shrink, leading to fierce public anger.
On Saturday, tens of thousands of people marched through the streets of Madrid to protest the eviction, some setting off flares. They carried placards reading “Not one more eviction, not one less neighbor, we are all Maricarmen” and “right to housing at a fair price.”
At the end of the march, protesters sat down in the Puerta del Sol plaza, some pitching tents. They remained in place early Sunday as dozens of activists staged a sit-in. A model of a vulture, decrying so-called “vulture funds,” hung above the camp.
Earlier in the week, tenants unions and other housing groups held protests and rallies in 16 cities, including Granada, Logroño and Zaragoza.
An investment fund acquired Abascal’s building in 2018 and sought a steep increase in her rent, and she had been fighting eviction for more than five years, according to the Madrid tenants union.
Duro said court officials and representatives of the fund, Urbagestión, had refused to suspend the eviction despite a pending court filing, humanitarian appeals and evidence that public authorities were working to secure alternative accommodation.
“They’re all inhumane,” Abascal said in a Spanish television interview the day before her eviction. “It’s as if I’m living with a machete at the back of my neck, ready to be chopped off at any moment.”
Duro also said an anonymous individual had offered to cover the rent payments, but the landlord declined to sign a new lease.
“We’ve been trying to negotiate with the landlords right up until the last moment, and they’ve flatly refused everything,” she said, decrying “a lack of humanity” in her treatment and “all these public resources” channeled into enabling the eviction.
Urbagestión did not respond to a request for comment.
The fresh wave of anger comes after protests in recent years against overtourism in Barcelona, where activists say a surge in apartments being used for short-term vacation rentals has contributed to a shortage of affordable housing.
The European Union announced new rules earlier this month aimed at tackling the housing crunch caused by short-term rentals in tourism hot spots.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described the eviction as “a social tragedy that we cannot accept either as a country or, of course, from the perspective of public institutions.”
Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Wednesday, Sánchez accused Madrid’s conservative regional government of pursuing luxury penthouses while ignoring demand for social housing.
Irene Hernández López, a 31-year-old test engineer living and renting in Chamberí, about 2 miles from Retiro, said what had happened to Abascal was “outrageous,” and she is worried similar evictions were already happening to other tenants around the city.
“Housing has become a product that people do business with,” she told NBC News. “It no longer matters that it’s your personal world, where you live and where you do your life.”
Hernández López, who pays 500 euros ($570) for a room in an apartment she shares with two others, said she was currently looking to move because the property was old and needs repairs, but that the rental market in Madrid was “terrible,” with prices “rising extremely quickly” and very little available.
“Some rooms are 500 euros or 600 euros and you think, ‘How am I supposed to live here? How can I pay 500 euros for this?’” she said. “I do think prices should be regulated, because wages aren’t going up while housing prices keep increasing. I don’t know how we’re supposed to keep going.”
Dan Nicander, secretary-general for the International Union of Tenants, said the situation in Spain was something his organization had seen in many countries in Europe.
“It’s a part of the financialization problem, seeing housing as an asset more than a home to people,” he told NBC News.
It’s “really tough” for the people living in the houses to do anything about it, he added, saying the responsibility lay with  politicians “to regulate the market in a way that it shouldn’t be that easy to buy and invest and then not [be] using the houses as homes.”
“Housing is a right,” he said. “It’s a fundamental right, first and foremost. It shouldn’t be a commodity.”
Jamie Gray is a senior desk editor for NBC News based in London.
Freddie Clayton is a freelance journalist based in London.

articles.title_zh: At least 27 people killed in two shootings in South African townships
articles.content_orig:
At least 27 people have been killed and more than 20 wounded in two shootings in two South African townships, according to police.
In the first incident late on Saturday, at least 17 people were killed and 15 wounded in a shooting at a tavern in Wedela southwest of Johannesburg.
Police said they were searching for eight suspects, who were “reportedly armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols”. The motive for the shooting remained unknown, and no arrests were announced.
Early on Sunday, gunmen killed at least 10 people and wounded 11 at a store in Lwandle near Cape Town.
The shootings took place just days after a shooting at a house party near the city of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.
In the first incident, police said the attack began about 9:30pm (19:30 GMT) on Saturday in Extension 3, Wedela, in Gauteng province’s West Rand district.
The gunmen fired at people gathered outside the tavern before going inside, where more shots were fired. Investigators said some customers were searched during the attack and had their mobile phones taken.
The suspects then escaped in two vehicles. Two other vehicles were burned during the incident.
Captain Tintswalo Sibeko said detectives and specialist police units had been assigned to identify and find the eight suspects, with police opening 17 murder cases and 15 attempted murder cases as well as two cases related to property damage.
In the second incident, police said they were searching for multiple suspects after the shooting that took place after midnight on Sunday.
South Africa records persistently high levels of violent crime, including killings involving firearms.
The government has faced sustained pressure to improve public safety, particularly in major urban areas where police have carried out additional operations against gun crimes.

articles.title_orig: Police declare major incident at UK's Fairford air base, used by US air forces
articles.title_zh: Police declare major incident at UK's Fairford air base, used by US air forces
articles.content_orig:
Several men have been arrested on suspicion of crimes related to explosives at a village near an air base used by U.S. forces, police in southwestern England said on Sunday.
Police in Gloucestershire said it had declared a major incident and evacuated "a number of properties" in the Whelford area following the arrest of "several men on suspicion of offences under the explosives act," referring to the country's laws around explosives.
The authorities also said a bomb disposal team were on site examining a number of vehicles.
Some local residents were evacuated, police said, and a cordon was established but the incident is said to be "contained."
The town of Whelford is close to RAF Fairford, a base that American forces have used for strictly limited strikes during the war with Iran. After the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran on Feb. 28, the U.K. government allowed the American military to use the Fairford base to strike Iranian missile sites.
However, police did not confirm to the Associated Press whether the arrests were linked to the base.
A spokesperson for the U.S. Air Force said its personnel based at RAF Fairford "remain vigilant" but would not discuss specific force protection measures for security reasons.
"We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families," the spokesperson said.
The U.S. military's European Command said it would not discuss specific force protection measures, but added it would "take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our U.S. service members, civilians, contractors, and their families across the European theater."
Security measures have been significantly increased in recent days at the air baise, according to an eyewitness quoted by the Reuters news agency who said there had been more roadblocks and armed police preventing access.
A spokesperson for the U.K. government thanked emergency services for acting quickly and added that it would be "inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing."
The Associated  Press contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: College football winners, losers in Week 4: Iowa emerges as Big Ten title threat, John Mateer struggles again
articles.title_zh: College football winners, losers in Week 4: Iowa emerges as Big Ten title threat, John Mateer struggles again
articles.content_orig:
Week 4 marks the formal start of conference play across college football , and the big-time matchups delivered. No. 17 Iowa pulled a stunner against No. 18 Michigan to win at Michigan Stadium for the first time since 2010 on the last play.
But while there's been plenty of highs, a few high-profile players struggled in big moments. Trinidad Chambliss was unable to keep up the magic against Florida , while Oklahoma's John Mateer collapsed against Georgia . The ACC race also took a wild turn after Wake Forest upset Louisville .
In the night slate, a few more titans fell as No. 12 USC, No. 13 Penn State and No. 23 Texas A&M all dropped. The losses shake up conference title and postseason pictures, but can teams recover? Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 4.
Expectations were low for the Aggies when they traveled to face No. 10 LSU. But in one fell swoop, a 35-6 loss, No. 23 Texas A&M's season effectively ended. Quarterback Marcel Reed was regrettably the primary culprit, completing a paltry 10 of 26 passes for 106 yards and an interception. The backup, Brady Hart, threw an interception on his only pass attempt.
As if that wasn't bad enough, Texas A&M allowed more than 300 yards passing and nearly 200 yards rushing. Frankly, the Aggies are just a bad football team at this point. Outside of a few talented wide receivers, who can't get the ball due to bad quarterback play, it's hard to find a single advantage Texas A&M can create against opponents.
No. 1 Texas, No. 8 Alabama and No. 14 Tennessee are still on the schedule, along with a road trip to Oklahoma. Will the Aggies make a bowl game?
The Cowboys officially turned the page on their season-opening loss to Tulsa by storming back from an early deficit to beat West Virginia 41-24 on the road. The Mountaineers were right on the edge of the rankings last week after beating No. 25 Virginia, and took a 14-3 lead early in the second quarter.
But when faced with adversity, quarterback Drew Mestemaker and wide receiver Wyatt Young again rose to the occasion. Young was unstoppable with eight catches for 192 yards and a touchdown in the win. Mestemaker shook off an interception to finish with 389 yards on only 27 pass attempts, 270 yards of which came in the second half.
The win over West Virginia was Oklahoma State's first Big 12 win in more than 1,000 days, snapping an 18-game losing streak. The last win was amazingly before the Cowboys played in the 2023 Big 12 title game. A new era is afoot.
Once again, USC was presented with the opportunity to get over the hump. After knocking Dante Moore out of the game with a dirty play, they were even playing at home against a backup quarterback. But when the game was decided, the Trojans were again too soft.
USC faced multiple opportunities to extend drives, but went 2 of 11 on third down. The Trojans failed to contain backup Dylan Raiola on fourth down and got bullied in high-leverage spots. This Trojans team is young, but excuses just keep piling up every year. With No. 5 Indiana, No. 7 Ohio State and No. 13 Penn State left on the schedule, when will it happen?
The Badgers needed something positive to happen in the Luke Fickell era. Old Dominion quarterback transfer Colton Joseph was ready to deliver. In the last 3:31, Joseph threw two touchdown passes to stun No. 13 Penn State, including a 72-yard pass to Jacob Harris with only 73 seconds remaining. It was the most complete defensive performance we've seen the Badgers put together, holding Penn State to only 233 yards. This was the kind of game Fickell was hired to win. There's a long season ahead, but can Fickell build on it?
Iowa's win against No. 18 Michigan to stay undefeated was a perfect Kirk Ferentz football game. The Hawkeyes puttered about for the first 40 minutes of play, only staying within striking distance because of a 99-yard kickoff return for a touchdown. And then, Hank Brown came to life.
The Hawkeyes got one of the great plays in program history, a game-winning touchdown with no time left on the clock by Brown to Reece Vander Zee for an unbelievable touchdown. The win was the first for Iowa in Michigan Stadium since 2010. More importantly, it seriously launched the No. 17 Hawkeyes into the Big Ten title and postseason conversation. With conference frontrunners Ohio State and Oregon already possessing losses, Iowa could easily crash the party.
Playing Georgia is never a recipe for success, but Oklahoma's QB1 put together one of the most stunningly poor performances of the season. After going down 14-0 in the second quarter, Mateer dropped one of the worst fumbles you'll ever see that turned third-and-goal into a Georgia defensive touchdown. He threw another interception, and then dropped the ball yet again to set up a short 11-yard touchdown drive for Georgia.
By the time the dust settled, Oklahoma was trailing 28-0 at halftime, part of a 41-13 loss against the Bulldogs in Athens. Statistically, Mateer was able to fight back in garbage time to finish with a respectable stat line, but the damage was done.
Oklahoma coach Brent Venables acknowledged that he considered making a change at halftime , but backup Whitt Newbauer has never played real snaps. There's no real answer on this Sooners roster, and Mateer is the face of the dysfunction.

The Gators announced their return to major college football under Jon Sumrall on Saturday, finishing off an emphatic 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss . The Gators obliterated the Rebels behind a combined 268 yards and four touchdowns rushing from Jadan Baugh and Duke Clark , finishing with more than 300 yards on the ground as a team.
While an emotional letdown was expected for the Rebels after the dramatic win over Lane Kiffin and LSU last weekend, Florida looks the part of a serious national contender for the first time in years. The Gators still have No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Georgia on the schedule, but the Florida team we saw in Week 4 can hang with anyone.
The Cardinals can't make anything easy. One week after taking control of the ACC championship race with a win over SMU, Louisville lost a stunner against a streaking Wake Forest squad 30-27. With the loss, the Cardinals are no longer an at-large contender for the College Football Playoff field with two early losses. SMU still has a shot, and there are a few loose undefeated ACC teams left, but Louisville looked like the top competition to Miami . Now, things are much more complicated.
Boise State officially took their place as kings of the Group of Six race after obliterating Western Michigan 32-7 in a marquee matchup. The Broncos were fantastic in the win, holding WMU to 3.8 yards per pass attempt and 2 of 11 on third down, while getting an efficient 204 yards and three touchdowns from Maddux Madsen . With wins over Memphis and Western Michigan, Boise State becomes the heavy favorite to reach the College Football Playoff -- if it can survive a stacked Pac-12.
Texas Tech put a lot of faith in Hammond coming off of an ACL tear, but the redshirt sophomore has struggled to meet the moment after taking over as the starter. Hammond threw three interceptions in the first half against Sam Houston and looked out of sorts as the Bearkats pulled within 21-14 at the half.
Hammond managed to get back on track in the second half, but it's been multiple games of inconsistent play for a team that hoped to contend for the Big 12 title. The running game got going in the second half, but teams just don't trust Hammond's downfield passing, and it's making life harder. The talent is there, but the consistency has to come soon with the heart of Big 12 play on the horizon.

articles.title_orig: Host Jalen Brunson gets assist from Knicks on 'SNL' premiere
articles.title_zh: Host Jalen Brunson gets assist from Knicks on 'SNL' premiere
articles.content_orig:
Knicks superstar Jalen Brunson becomes just the 5th NBA player to host the iconic late-night show.
The synergy creates New York autumn magic.
Jalen Brunson, who led the New York Knicks to the 2026 NBA championship – the team’s first title since 1973 – and was named Finals MVP, hosted the season opener of “ Saturday Night Live” on NBC Saturday, just before the Knicks open training camp and begin their quest for another title.
We’re LIVE with Jalen Brunson and KATSEYE on @nbc and @peacock ! pic.twitter.com/820Yar5kST
— Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) September 27, 2026
first read-thru of the season with @jalenbrunson1 !!! pic.twitter.com/yAohsZsbn7
— Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) September 24, 2026
What a great night it was for New Yorkers, the Knicks and their fans, Brunson and SNL , which is shot in NBC’s Studio 8H at 30 Rockefeller Plaza in midtown Manhattan.
Brunson will join Bill Russell, Michael Jordan, Charles Barkley and LeBron James as the only people with deep NBA connections to host SNL . Jordan, Barkley (in his first of four times hosting) and James were active players when they hosted, and Russell was between NBA coaching jobs when he hosted.
SNL ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/vyQfbsMg0x
— Karl-Anthony Towns (@KarlTowns) September 27, 2026
With Brunson hosting the opener of the show’s 52 nd season, here’s a look at the NBA stars who have hosted SNL:
After a cold open in this season 5 episode, Russell delivered his monologue, a riff on the teamwork required to win in the NBA and the teamwork required to make a great episode of SNL – with a big man in the middle of it all necessary for both to excel.
He appeared in several skits, including one with Bill Murray who played a sports radio talk-show host who knew nothing about basketball – while promoting Russell’s actual book Second Wind .
Russell was a serious man, especially about basketball and social justice, but he loved to laugh and hearing that Russell cackle was always a delight.
So happy for @jalenbrunson1 ! My Dad, Bill Russell, was the first NBA player to host! https://t.co/acrW6e26ZL pic.twitter.com/BzPLMUCyIQ
— Karen Kenyatta Russell🍀 (@Karen_Russell) September 9, 2026
Jordan was coming off his first NBA championship, and his stardom was skyrocketing when he was the guest host for the season 17 opener. Wearing sunglasses for his monologue, Jordan brought his trademark swagger to the set and allowed SNL writers to push comedy boundaries.
The highlight of Jordan’s skits in this episode was his bit on Stuart Smalley’s Daily Affirmations . Played by Al Franken, Smalley tries to boost his insufficient self-esteem by looking into a mirror and acknowledging “I’m good enough, I’m smart enough and doggone it, people like me.”
With Jordan sitting next to him, Franken’s character says, “I can imagine a night before a game, you must lie awake thinking, ‘I’m not good enough. Everybody’s better than me. I’m not going to score any points. I have no business playing this game.’ ”
“Well, not really,” Jordan replied.
By the end of the skit, Jordan looks in the mirror, barely containing his laughter and repeats what Smalley says: “I don’t have to be a great basketball player. I don’t have to dribble the ball fast or throw the ball into the basket. Because all I have to do is be the best Michael I can be. Because I’m good enough, I’m smart enough and doggone it, people like me.”
Musical guest: Public Enemy
Barkley is a natural in front of the camera, and he has the comedic chops to warrant his SNL appearances. His first guest host duties came in the season 19 opener – just a few months after Jordan’s Bulls defeated Barkley’s Phoenix Suns in the NBA Finals. Barkley was also just a few months removed from earning the regular-season MVP award.
For that episode, Barkley cut a promo with Nirvana, saying, “Hi, I’m Charles Barkley, host of the season premiere of “Saturday Night Live” with Nirvana. Look mom, your favorite, Nirvana” with Kurt Cobain, Dave Grohl and Krist Novoselic standing in the shot.
Twenty-five years later, he hosted for the fourth time. There’s a reason the show has asked him back – he’s a good sport about it, able to poke fun while allowing the SNL writers to poke fun at him.
Musical guests: Nirvana, Alicia Keys, Kelly Clarkson, Migos
Getting ready to start his fifth NBA season, James was just 22 years old – he hadn’t yet won his first MVP or first title – when he hosted the opener of SNL’s 33 rd season.
He entered the set for his monologue, dancing to center stage and cracked a joke, “For those of you who don’t watch basketball, this past season we went to the NBA Finals, and we swept the San Antonio Spurs in four games, and for those of you who do watch basketball, be cool and shut up. There’s no reason to ruin it for everybody else.”
He was also a natural, appearing in several humorous skits including a good one with Bill Hader and Jason Sudeikis. James has carved out a little slice of the entertainment world with several shows and movies he has produced and appeared in, including Space Jam: A New Legacy and a role alongside Hader and Amy Schumer in Trainwreck.
“To be a part of the “Saturday Night Live” legacy is something that’s a dream come true,” James said at the 2025 NBA All-Star Game . “It’s been on, obviously, my entire life, and seeing so many great actors grace those skits every single Saturday and so many entertainers that come there and do their bits, as well, it was fun. It was super fun, and hopefully I get the opportunity to do it again. I would love to do it again. I was so young.”

articles.title_orig: UFC fighter Barcelos 'stable, alert' after TKO loss in main event
articles.title_zh: UFC fighter Barcelos 'stable, alert' after TKO loss in main event
articles.content_orig:
The UFC Vegas 121 main event clash between Raoni Barcelos and Raul Rosas Jr. ended in scary fashion in the fifth round when the Brazilian bantamweight went unconscious for apparent no reason during a clinch exchange. Barcelos was rushed to the hospital for exams after the bout, and his head coach Davi Ramos shared on social media he is now back to his senses.
The UFC released a statement hours after the incident to confirm Barcelos was transported to a Level 1 trauma center for evaluation and was "stable, alert and responsive, with full movement" after a "CT scan and comprehensive assessment" were conducted.
"Raoni is doing well," Ramos said in Portuguese on a video posted on social media. "He has all his senses, he's moving his leg, his arm, his hand, he's conscious, he's talking, everything is fine with him. He's undergoing some tests, and pretty soon he'll be here to talk to you guys."
"I just wanted to let you know so you can all stay calm," he continued. "Keep praying for him. He's undergoing all the tests that are standard in a situation like this. He'll have to rest because of what happened, but God willing, everything will be fine. He'll be here with us soon and he'll be talking to you guys. Thank you to everyone who's been sending messages, positive energy, praying and keeping all of us in your prayers."
Barcelos was up in all three scorecards going into the final round, including a 10-8 in round four for one of the judges, meaning he was a little over three minutes away from a decision victory. The loss snapped what would be his sixth straight victory in the UFC.
"We had a great fight," Ramos said. "We practice a sport that we can't predict, unfortunately, but we know for sure that we were doing our best. Raoni is a warrior, a phenomenal fighter, and he showed you that with all the technique he has, all the skill and heart he has. He showed everything about where he wants to go, where we all want to go, with all the work we've been putting in. Congratulations to him, and thank you all for the messages. Keep praying for him, and pretty soon he'll be back here with us to put on another great show."

articles.title_orig: Jon Watts to Direct Next ‘Star Wars’ Movie
articles.title_zh: Jon Watts to Direct Next ‘Star Wars’ Movie
articles.content_orig:
A new “ Star Wars ” movie is currently in development with director Jon Watts attached.
Watts is best known for directing the popular “Spider-Man” trilogy starring Tom Holland, which includes 2017’s Spider-Man: Homecoming,” 2019’s “Spider-Man: Far From Home,” and 2021’s “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” (2026’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” was directed by Destin Daniel Cretton.) Before being selected to direct “Spider-Man,” Watts also helmed films including “Cop Car” and “Clown.” Following his involvement with the trilogy, In 2024, it was reported that Watts, his production company Freshman Year and producer Dianne McGunigle had signed a first-look feature deal with Walt Disney Studios.
In 2024, Watts co-created “Skeleton Crew” alongside Christopher Ford, a coming-of-age series set in the era of the New Republic that followed four young characters on a new adventure, per the show’s official logline. Jude Law starred as Jod Na Nawood, with Ravi Cabot-Conyers as Wim, Ryan Kiera Armstrong as Fern, Kyriana Kratter as KB and Robert Timothy Smith as Neel.
With the role, Watts joins a list of previous “Star Wars” directors that includes Irvin Kershner, Richard Marquand, J.J. Abrams, Rian Johnson and “Star Wars” creator George Lucas. Released in 2019, Abrams’ “Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker” is the most recent film in the franchise to debut theatrically.
As previously reported by Variety , Simon Kinberg will pen the script for the film. Kinberg is best known for being a writer, producer and director for the “X-Men” franchise, and was considered a surprising choice at the time of the announcement.
Knight Edge Media first broke the news.

articles.title_orig: A Storied Indian Business Empire Is Being Torn Apart by Infighting
articles.title_zh: A Storied Indian Business Empire Is Being Torn Apart by Infighting
articles.content_orig:
New Delhi, India – An unprecedented power struggle has erupted at the top of one of India’s largest conglomerates, pitting the board of its holding company Tata Sons against its majority shareholder Tata Trusts.
Last week, Tata Sons extended Chairman N Chandrasekaran’s term and said it would consider publicly listing the holding company, flying in the face of the family charity that controls the 158-year-old Tata Group.
Extending Chandrasekaran’s chairmanship and taking Tata public is at the heart of the family-linked feud – and its outcome will not be limited merely to the group’s headquarters at Bombay House.
Collectively, listed Tata companies have a market capitalisation of $277bn and influence over 17.7 million retail shareholders apart from pension funds, insurers and mutual funds, investment advisory firm InGovern said.
So what’s behind the bitter brawl inside one of the corporate world’s most consequential boardrooms?
The Tata Group business conglomerate spans industries from information technology and automobiles to steel, power, aviation, chemicals and consumer goods.
It has 26 publicly listed companies, including TCS and Tata Motors. They have a combined market capitalisation of $277bn and operate across more than 100 countries. Tata Sons serves as the group’s principal holding and investment company.
The group’s humble beginnings go back more than 150 years when Nusserwanji Tata, born into a Parsi priest’s family in Gujarat, moved to Mumbai (then Bombay) in the mid-19th century and entered the trading business.
He later expanded into trade with China before his son Jamsetji Tata built the business into an industrial group, riding on deals in cotton and opium. Opium was then banned by China’s Qing rulers, and Nusserwanji found a way to smuggle it.
The conglomerate’s real breakthrough came when the United States Civil War broke out in 1861. The disruption to US cotton supplies sent Indian cotton prices soaring and transformed the fortunes of Bombay’s merchants, including the Tatas.
Their businesses turned into an empire over coming generations. Jamsetji Tata died in 1904, and his sons Dorabji and Ratanji Tata carried his businesses forward. The family’s charitable trusts became major shareholders of Tata Sons.
JRD Tata, who became chairman in 1938, transformed the group into a diversified industrial enterprise, expanding into aviation, including India’s flagship carrier, Air India; chemicals; and engineering. In 1991, Ratan Tata succeeded JRD, taking over as India began economic liberalisation.
Under Ratan, the Tata Group consolidated a sprawling group under a more unified corporate identity and pushed it onto the global stage with landmark acquisitions, including Tetley, Corus and Jaguar Land Rover. Tata is now pushing into the next generation of global manufacturing with a major iPhone assembly operation in India and a semiconductor fabrication and chip-assembly business.
Ratan was the chairman of both Tata Sons and its majority stakeholder, Tata Trusts, and remained a bridge between the two. After he died in 2024, a widening schism gradually became apparent.
Tata Trusts is an umbrella of family-linked charities that own 66 percent of Tata Sons.
The face-off was triggered on September 17 when Tata Sons reappointed Chandrasekaran as its chairman over the Tata Trusts’ nominee on the board, Noel Tata, in a 4-to-1 vote.
Noel Tata is the sitting chairman of Tata Trusts and the only family-linked senior executive sitting in the top echelons of Tata Sons today. Noel is the half-brother of Ratan Tata and became Tata Trusts’ chairman after Ratan’s death in 2024.
But the divisions between the company and majority shareholder run deeper – and include questions of taking Tata Sons public and providing a planned exit to Tata Sons’ second-largest shareholder, Shapoorji Pallonji.
Last month, Chandrasekaran said he would not seek another term as chairman after February 2027. But Tata Group said in a statement the board asked him to reconsider the group’s “larger interests”, a request that he accepted.
The 68-year-old Noel Tata called the reappointment “illegal” under Tata Sons’ articles of association, adding in a statement that both trust nominees on the board were required to vote in coordination, whereas only Noel Tata voted against. The other trust nominee, Venu Srinivasan, voted in favour of Chandrasekaran’s reappointment.
This matter is now expected to be decided by the courts.
India’s central bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), requires companies with assets exceeding $10.45bn to publicly list.
Tata Sons tried to skirt the requirements by deregistering as a nonbank finance company. But days before its board meeting this month, the RBI rejected the company’s request, bringing it closer to a public listing.
Tata’s structure is unusual because the holding company at the very top of the empire is at the moment not itself subject to public-market scrutiny, even though many of the companies beneath it are.
At the board meeting, Tata Sons said it would take steps to comply with the RBI’s requirements. But Noel Tata opposed the move, arguing that listing would alter the character of a group that also supports extensive philanthropic ⁠activities.
The Shapoorji Pallonji Group holds ⁠an 18.4 percent stake in Tata Sons and is its second-largest shareholder.
The infrastructure and construction conglomerate is knee-deep in debt and is seeking ⁠to monetise its shareholding in Tata Sons.
Tata Trusts said Noel Tata tabled a plan to sell ‌a part of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group’s stake in the holding company worth $2.61bn. Tata Sons has not yet commented on the plan.
Shapoor Mistry, the group’s patriarch, is also Noel Tata’s brother-in-law. The Shapoorji Pallonji Group backs Tata Sons going public and is opposed to Noel’s position.
The central question in the showdown that is captivating millions of Indians involves the public listing of Tata Sons.
Noel Tata said in a statement that the Tata Group “was conceived as a national service carried on through business”. The unusual privately owned structure of Tata Sons, Noel argued, has allowed the company to remain in the country’s service and “act repeatedly in ways that a purely commercial calculus would not have supported”.
“A listing will destroy its character and strike at the heart of this principle,” Tata Trusts has argued.
However, Santosh Mehrotra, an Indian development economist, told Al Jazeera that Tata Sons needs to be listed publicly, no matter what. “There is a law for everyone, and Tata cannot be an exception to that,” he said.
“We are at a stage as a country when top business houses cannot be allowed to continue to behave in whatever manner they have managed to behave in over the last 100 years,” Mehrotra said.
Mehrotra argued that over the past decade under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India’s top business houses, including the empires of billionaires Gauran Adani and Mukesh Ambani, “have been permitted by the government to grow the concentration of industries across sectors in a historically unprecedented manner”.
“India’s biggest business houses have grown horizontally, capturing all sectors, which have come at the cost of people below them in the pyramid,” Mehrotra said.
“That means that the core inflation is being driven essentially by these handful of businesses because their horizontal and vertical control gives them the ability to mock up prices that are unprecedented in our economy’s history while their profits mount,” he said.
Mehrotra said that while the Tata boardroom drama could be captivating for some, “ordinary Indians’ concerns are rooted in regulating the unchecked growth [of conglomerates] backed by the government.”

Celebrating Mass at the Shrine of Our Lady of Lourdes on Sunday, the third day of his apostolic journey to France, Pope Leo XIV said the gathering of pilgrims from France and around the world revealed âthe universal face of the Church,â and he encouraged them to bring âthe consolation of Lourdesâ back to their homes and communities.
Reflecting on the Sunday readings and the message entrusted by the Virgin Mary to Saint Bernadette, the Pope placed conversion at the heart of his homily.
âToday, not tomorrow, that we must repent,â he said, explaining that God desires people to âopen our eyes and return to him.â Conversion, he explained, means leaving behind paths on which we have lost our way and choosing âthe way of life.â
Pope Leo recalled Maryâs words to Saint Bernadette: âI do not promise to make you happy in this world but in the next.â In a society focused on progress and material wellbeing, he said, Lourdes recalls the dignity of every human life and the hope of eternal life.
âIn the face of current trends that seek to redefine the value of human life in illness, suffering and old age, the grotto of Massabielle stands as a place of Christian hope,â he said. At Lourdes, he added, crutches, wheelchairs and âhidden tearsâ are not obstacles but places where people can encounter Godâs love.
The Pope also recalled Maryâs repeated call at Lourdes: âPenance! Penance! Penance!â, noting that Mary asked Bernadette to undertake acts of penance not only for herself but also âfor sinners.â
Linking this appeal to the conflicts and suffering present in the world today, he asked: âHow can our hearts not be moved by the conflicts that are spreading and destroying so many innocent lives?â
Yet, he continued, the roots of evil are found in the human heart. âIt is therefore human hearts that must change, beginning with our own.â
âIt is therefore human hearts that must change, beginning with our own,â he said, stressing that penance is âan act of love, carried out in solidarity with the human family.â
That call to conversion, Pope Leo said, applies to the Church herself.
âShe must have the courage to begin with herself,â he said, calling for humility in confronting the Churchâs âdeep wounds, infidelities and painful errors.â Recognising faults, he added, is essential to spiritual growth.
And citing Saint Augustine, he said, âDo not be content with what you are, if you want to become what you are not yet.â
The Pope then turned particularly to those who are sick, telling them that their suffering can become a participation in Christâs redemptive work.
âDear friends who are sick, so many of you here in Lourdes are familiar with suffering,â he said. Their trials and pains, when lived in a spirit of offering, can contribute to âthe redemptive work that the world so greatly needs.â
âIn this way,â Pope Leo added, âyou are truly at the heart of the Church, and your role is irreplaceable.â
Pope Leo concluded by telling pilgrims that they would leave Lourdes changed by their encounter with Mary and with one another.
âYou will not leave Lourdes as you arrived. You will leave as missionaries of hope,â he said, adding that âThe miracle of Lourdesâ is that it can âawaken the joy of hope in the very midst of suffering and hardship.â

articles.title_orig: Trump tells female MS Now reporter to ‘be quiet’ amid questions on press pool ban
articles.title_zh: Trump tells female MS Now reporter to ‘be quiet’ amid questions on press pool ban
articles.content_orig:
US president doubles down on criticism of CNN and MS Now as Akayla Gardner questions attempted White House ban
A day after the White House barred CNN from traveling aboard Air Force One to provide pool television coverage of the president’s trip to Tennessee, Donald Trump doubled down on his criticism of that broadcaster and another, MS Now, he has attempted to ban over coverage of him he calls overly negative.
As he left the White House early on Saturday, Trump was asked by MS Now White House correspondent Akayla Gardner: “Do you only want outlets that support you to be a part of the press pool?”
“No, no, no. I want real news, not fake news – like you,” Trump replied, in a moment that was not broadcast live, due to the removal of CNN as the designated pool television crew, but was posted on social media by the White House.
As Trump continued on, repeating past insults about CNN and MS Now, which he called “MS DNC”, in reference to the Democratic National Committee, Gardner pressed him harder: “Do you not want tough questions?”
“Be quiet,” Trump said, before continuing to air his familiar grievance that their reporting on him is not flattering enough.
Since his first presidency, Trump has labeled nonpartisan news outlets that do not openly support him “the enemy of the people”, maligning unfavorable reports as “fake news”. In his second term, he has increasingly told female reporters who ask him challenging questions to be quiet.
Tensions with the press corps soared to new heights last weekend, when administration officials revoked the White House credentials of MS Now, Politico and CNN after Trump announced what he himself called a “ban on the free press”.
A federal judge temporarily restored access for the blacklisted outlets on Thursday, but that evening MS Now and CNN reporters and producers were prevented by Trump’s aides from covering his state dinner in honor of Chinese president Xi Jinping.
On Friday, the White House removed CNN from a rotation of television networks charged with covering presidential travel. The White House Correspondents’ Association previously coordinated pool assignments, but the administration seized control of choosing which network provides pool television coverage each day during Trump’s second presidency.
CNN had been scheduled to accompany Trump on Saturday, as he visited Knoxville, Tennessee, for a college football game.
Real America’s Voice, a pro-Trump network that lacks the technical capability to provide live video for other broadcasters, instead accompanied the president during the brief trip. The partisan, rightwing network shared a limited number of clips of the trip on social media, including video of Trump’s image being displayed on the stadium’s big screen, which it captioned : “PRESIDENT TRUMP LIGHTS UP THE JUMBOTRON”.
Trump returned to Washington DC on Saturday afternoon without taking questions from the print reporters who were permitted to accompany him.
“He is picking a fight with the people who are telling unpleasant truths about his administration,” Brian Stelter, CNN’s chief media analyst, said on air about the network’s exclusion from Air Force One. “Today, yes, it happens to be CNN, but tomorrow it could be any other news outlet.”

It happened at 700 Euclid Ave. in the East New York section.
Police sources told Eyewitness News that a 56-year-old man was walking through a parking lot when he was struck by the falling tree.

He was taken to Brookdale Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
The incident happened during the nor'easter, which brought damaging wind gusts, but it's not known whether the wind caused the tree to fall.
Also in Brooklyn, at least four people were injured by a falling tree around 5:30 p.m. at East 14thStreet and Avenue S at Kelly Park Playground in the Homecrest section.

articles.title_zh: Why Xi Jinping skipped the UN after his Trump summit
articles.content_orig:
China touts multilateralism and growing soft power even as Beijing gives greater weight to its relationship with Washington
Han Zheng, China’s vice-president, called on “major countries” to respect the sovereignty and security of Middle Eastern nations and bring about a two-state solution for the “Palestinian question” on Saturday at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in an implicit dig at the US and Israel.
“Many months ago, Chinese officials said that Xi wouldn’t go to the UN unless it was to mark a major anniversary,” said Bonnie Glaser, managing director of the German Marshall Fund of the United States. “Seems like a missed opportunity.”
Since coming to power in 2012, Xi has addressed the annual General Assembly gathering once in person, in 2015 for the 70th anniversary. He appeared by video in 2020 and 2021 during the pandemic but missed the 80th anniversary last year when Premier Li Qiang spoke. In other years, China has generally been represented by other senior officials, including Han and Foreign Minister Wang Yi.

articles.title_orig: Trump says he ended Biden electric vehicle rule, updated fuel economy standards
articles.title_zh: Trump says he ended Biden electric vehicle rule, updated fuel economy standards
articles.content_orig:
The Trump administration is planning to release new fuel efficiency mandates Monday that would weaken stringent rules implemented under President Biden.
President Trump pitched the changes, which he announced in December, as a way to boost the domestic auto industry and lower consumer costs. He made the original announcement standing alongside several auto executives.
“These new Standards will take the waste out of building cars in America,” Trump said in a social media post Saturday. “That means LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands on a new, beautiful, and safe car — Far better than the Environmental Monsters that we were building heretofore.”
Trump has long criticized the Biden-era rules, which were part of a set of policies to spur production and purchases of electric vehicles. EV production and sales have plummeted as a consequence of Trump administration policies, and the new changes also come as elevated fuel prices are sending ripples through the broader U.S. economy.
Trump, whose party is struggling in the polls ahead of the November midterm elections, has been under pressure to do more to address concerns about rising prices for consumer goods, particularly as oil prices have remained persistently high since the start of the Iran war.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy responded to the president’s comments Saturday with his own social media post, saying that a “major victory for America’s auto workers is COMING MONDAY.” A U.S. official confirmed that new Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards will be released Monday.
If Monday’s final rule mirrors the original proposal from last year, it would lower the fuel-economy requirement for 2031 model-year vehicles to 34.5 miles per gallon from about 50 mpg previously.
The lowered standards would represent a major win for the auto and oil industries that complained the Biden-era requirements push the bounds of available technology and effectively discourage the sale of traditional gasoline-powered vehicles in favor of electric models.
However, the changes also come as diesel prices set a record high and gasoline prices reached their highest level ever for September, extending a rally driven by the Iran war and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
Trump administration officials are studying a range of options aimed at curbing soaring fuel prices, fueled in part by political impetus as rising cost of living is undermining Republicans’ odds of retaining control of Congress after the November midterm elections. Banning diesel exports has been floated as an option, though energy experts say such a step would only offer short-term relief and eventually drive costs even higher.
“With Americans struggling to afford gasoline that is more than $4 a gallon, the Trump administration is going to force them to pay more at the pump,” said Atid Kimelman, an attorney at Natural Resources Defense Council, an environmental nonprofit group. “Oil companies will get a windfall from gutting the fuel economy standards, but the rest of us are going to be handing over more of our hard-earned paychecks to fill up the tank.”
Mijares Torres writes for Bloomberg. Bloomberg writer Ari Natter contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Burnham vows to fix social care after father’s death
articles.title_zh: Burnham vows to fix social care after father’s death
articles.content_orig:
Andy Burnham has promised to fix the country’s broken social care system after his father died with Alzheimer’s disease.
The Prime Minister said that the experiences of Catherine Murray, his grandmother, and Roy Burnham, his father, in social care had motivated him to make it a priority.
He told the Sunday Mirror that the system going unfixed – from his time as a health secretary in Gordon Brown’s government to his father’s death this month – was the result of political cowardice.
Mr Burnham’s father died on Sept 14 , 24 years after Murray died having sold her home to pay for social care. The Prime Minister said that his father’s illness meant he did not know his son had become the UK’s leader.
Mr Burnham’s promise, delivered from his No 10 North office in Manchester on the eve of the Labour Party conference, expanded the vow he made when he took office to “expend quite a lot of political capital” on the issue .
“I saw what happened to my grandmother. You’re going back 25 years ago now. She died in 2002, and she went through the care system, and it wasn’t good enough at all. And that really focused me on the issue,” he said.
“But here I am today, having now directly, painfully, personally experienced the fact that that has happened to my parents’ generation, and not just [my parents], I’m talking about thousands and thousands of people across the country.
“That is a shameful dereliction of duty by a generation of Westminster politicians who have just shown total cowardice in relation to this issue.
“The idea that it’s too difficult. How can the care that we give from one person to another be too difficult for politics? How?
“I mean, that is terrible, that politics has got itself to a position where it’s so superficial and so focus-group-driven that it won’t take on a difficult argument and say, no we have to fix this.”
Mr Burnham is to give a speech at the conference on Tuesday, and is expected to address social care .
Despite not having a “complete detailed plan yet”, he said he wanted to use the speech to “make the argument in a front-foot way”.
He added: “You cannot fix 21st-century care needs on that basis where there’s no prevention and we’re just sending everything to hospital.
“In the end, it will sink the NHS if we carry on in this way. So I’m not going to leave office having done what everyone else in my position has done, and pretty much say: ‘Well, I’m not going to deal with this. It’s too difficult. It’s not a priority.’
“It is a priority for me, and I will face it. And it may make me unpopular, but I’m going to do it.”

High-stakes discussions on trade and artificial intelligence unfold in New York City as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer meet with Chinese officials. Fox News contributor Dan Hoffman analyzes this strategic framework between the world's two most powerful nations ahead of the upcoming summit with President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
The United States and China agreed to lower tariffs on $30 billion in goods traded between the two countries after a three-day summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C.
According to the White House, the $30 billion in reciprocal tariff reductions apply to "non-sensitive goods."
U.S. exports, including agricultural products, fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices will receive favorable tariff treatment in China. Meanwhile, U.S. imports of Chinese-made small appliances, toys, holiday decorations and children's car seats will also receive preferential treatment.
The agreement was reached through the U.S.-China Board of Trade, a body first proposed during Trump's visit to China in May and formally established during Xi's visit to Washington this week.
President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to speak during a state dinner in the East Room of the White House Sept. 24, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
XI PRAISES US STATE VISIT 'PERFECTION' AS TRUMP CALLS MEETINGS 'VERY PRODUCTIVE'
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC Friday that "a lot more details" about the new trade agreement will be released Monday.
Greer said the tariff terms were hammered out after weeks of negotiations. Neither country has released the final tariff rates or all the products that will receive favored status going forward.
This marks one of the most significant cooldowns in the trade war Trump launched against China in February 2025, when he levied a 10% tariff on all Chinese imports, citing Beijing's alleged role in the fentanyl crisis and illegal immigration. China hit back with levies on U.S. coal, liquefied natural gas, crude oil and cars.
President Donald Trump holds up a tariff chart while speaking during a "Make America Wealthy Again" trade announcement event in the Rose Garden at the White House April 2, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)
BESSENT REVEALS EXTENSION TO BUSAN AGREEMENT WITH CHINA UNTIL JANUARY
At their peak, U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods reached a staggering 145% in April 2025, shortly after Trump unveiled his "Liberation Day" reciprocal tariffs. China responded with tariffs of up to 125% on U.S. goods.
U.S. and Chinese negotiators met in Geneva in May 2025 and agreed to a 90-day truce that lowered U.S. tariffs to 30% and China's to 10%. The agreement was extended for another 90 days in August.
President Donald Trump walks on a red carpet after greeting Chinese President Xi Jinping during an arrival ceremony Sept. 23, 2026, at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

The two countries will now use the Board of Trade to negotiate additional tariff reductions and other trade disputes, leaving open the possibility of broader agreements in the months ahead.

articles.title_orig: Minecraft Dungeons II’s New Dimension Coming to Minecraft Java & Bedrock Edition
articles.title_zh: Minecraft Dungeons II’s New Dimension Coming to Minecraft Java & Bedrock Edition
articles.content_orig:
We’ve visited the Overworld, the Nether, and the End. Now, prepare yourself for a journey to the Sift.
First announced at Gamescom and showcased in more detail at Minecraft LIVE today, The Sift is the first new dimension in Minecraft in over 14 years, and players will be able to visit it in just a few days, when Minecraft Dungeons II launches on September 29.
But on top of that, Mojang Studios confirmed that the Sift will come to Minecraft in 2027, offering an entire new dimension for you to explore, survive, and create within.
In the opening stages of Minecraft Dungeons II , players will realize something is amiss. Strange events begin to upend the natural order of the Overworld, new enemy types appear, and souls begin to fly through the world. You’ve stumbled on the Sift.
This new reality brings an entirely different, colorful new look, new mobs (both companions and threats, all unique) and, once you enter, new rules to learn. Shifting tides within the Sift can affect your character and those around you; hazardous new blocks will alter how you approach exploration; new environments will put your skills to the test.
The Sift contains new biomes – including Meadows and Carapace – but Mojang are keeping other areas a secret for players to discover when they play Minecraft Dungeons II .
All of this will get seasoned players thinking about how Minecraft itself will change once the Sift arrives. While Mojang isn’t talking too much about how to access the Sift, or how it will stand out from Dungeons II ’s expression of it, we did get a brief in-development look at the new dimension running.
Suffice it to say, if you want a sneak peek at how the Sift will work, the best way to find out more is to play Dungeons II , which will give us a taste of mobs, blocks, and biomes . And make sure to tune in for future Minecraft LIVE events to learn more about the Sift, and when it will arrive.
Minecraft Dungeons II launches September 29 for XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, and will be included with Game Pass. Play it on both console and PC at no additional cost with XBOX Play Anywhere. Also available on Steam, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2.

articles.title_orig: ‘Charming and disarming’ … how Meta’s technology-packed Muse harnesses the power of cuteness
articles.title_zh: ‘Charming and disarming’ … how Meta’s technology-packed Muse harnesses the power of cuteness
articles.content_orig:
The tech giant has launched a cute ‘little guy’ that can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop
After the recent backlash against Meta’s so-called “pervert” smart glasses, this week Mark Zuckerberg launched a much cuter alternative: the Muse “charm” device.
With a screen that shows a cutesy little avatar, it has drawn comparisons with Tamagotchis. “We’ve packed a lot of technology into this little guy,” the Meta founder told the San Francisco audience .
The “little guy” could fit, like a Labubu, on to a keychain or bag. But unlike a Labubu, the interactive AI assistant will have significant capabilities, including the ability to have live conversations. It can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop.
According to Katie Seaborn, a Cambridge associate professor who has been researching cuteness – creating the science of cute voices within the context of computing – it’s cute because it “basically looks like a baby”.
For Joshua Paul Dale, professor at Chuo University in Tokyo and author of Irresistible: How Cuteness Wired our Brains and Conquered the World : “It’s really significant that along with the wearable charm, Meta also introduced a new pair of smart glasses with no camera. Everyone hates cameras in smart glasses. But if the camera is contained in a charm you wear around your neck, it shifts the agency. Suddenly, you’re not recording people. It’s just a cute little animated avatar looking out on the world.”
An individualised, customisable, and in this case adorable, AI companion, it tracks with Zuckerberg’s commitment to the idea of personal, wearable super-intelligence that you can chat to. As well as a broader shift towards cute technology , cited by forecasters WGSN as a top trend for 2026.
“Clearly,” says Dale, “what Meta is trying to do is make Muse into a companion. And it’s doing it in the simplest possible way … It’s using a very simplified, tiny 2-inch screen to encourage you to anthropomorphise the figure on it so that you treat it as if it’s human even though you know it’s not.”
Its cuteness is, according to Seaborn, “strategic”. “It’s very natural to emerge from this controversy with a technology that uses cuteness because … it’s so weak. Don’t worry about it. You can trust us.”
To try to harness the power of cuteness, according to Seaborn, “makes sense, especially from a big tech perspective because maybe people are getting wise to the ways of current strategies when it comes to people’s attention, their personal data and what have you. And now they’re trying new things that may or may not work”.
Seaborn, who has just moved to the University of Cambridge from Japan, points out that “this is something that is very normal in Japan. So the first thing you notice when you go there is that every single thing has a mascot. The government organisations, the media companies, the businesses, they all have a cute mascot”.
Seaborn has studied the “impacts cuteness can have on people”. “We’ve been seeing cuteness applied as a design strategy for different purposes. We know [that it] has certain impacts on people.” For one thing “cuteness is a way for certain social interactions to take place or to be smoothed over”.
There is also a “natural link between cuteness and deception … I call it ‘charming and disarming’, because one of the things cuteness does to us unconsciously, it’s just how our brain processes it, is lets down our guard. We can’t really help it.”
Whether Muse will catch on when it is released in December, or whether such a blatant attempt to gain trust via an on-screen avatar with cheeks you want to squish will land, remains to be seen. But different generations are likely to react differently. “That’s so AI!” is the phrase gen Alpha are using to dismiss anything they think is inauthentic.
For many gen Zers who are au fait with having a cuddly toy hanging from their bags , most typically in the form of a Labubu, it might feel less of a wrench. For older generations there will be nostalgic associations given its resemblance to older technologies. Embedded in it, says Seaborn, “[is] this legacy of these cute kind of gamified pet sort of things like Tamagotchi and Pocky Pikachu”.
Plus different cultural contexts will affect how it is received. Seaborn’s research has found that “Americans were actually less likely to be deceived compared with Japanese people … Because in Japan robots are heroes, they’re like babies”. Whereas “in western culture they’re often presented in the public imagination as kind of scary, potentially broken, sinister devices”. In UK focus groups, people reported a “gut feeling” that something was wrong when cuteness was part of a deceptive design idea. “People felt like something was off, but they couldn’t articulate what it was.”
But the picture, says Seaborn, is changing. “Because cuteness [or kawaii ] has been a cultural export of Japan and other nations for a while now … there might be a slow cultural shift happening in terms of how we orient ourselves towards cuteness and what we accept as adults.”
While Dale is “not rushing out to buy one”, he “will say, however, that when I’m 80 years old I’ll definitely want one of these things. I want to wear it around my neck always, and I want the camera on all the time, so it can tell me where I left my glasses.”

articles.title_zh: ‘Avengers: Endgame’ Snapping Up $26M at Box Office Amid Crowded Weekend
articles.content_orig:
Senior Entertainment Reporter
Avengers: Endgame looks to make a heroic return to the box office during a crowded frame that sees Resident Evil still carrying bite in its second week.
Marvel Studios ‘ 2019 blockbuster heads back to 3,060 North American screens with Avengers Endgame: Encore , which grossed around $11.2 million on Friday, including Thursday previews, and is expected to open at the top of the domestic chart with $26 million. Disney’s rerelease includes an exclusive look at footage from Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Doomsday , set to hit theaters Dec. 18.
During its initial run, Joe and Anthony Russo’s Endgame launched in April 2019 to a record-setting opening weekend of $1.2 billion globally. It went on to claim No. 2 on the all-time worldwide chart with a total run of $2.7 billion.
Sony’s Resident Evil still has teeth at second place with $6.9 million on Friday as it looks to collect $23.5 million domestically in its sophomore frame. Starring Austin Abrams, director Zach Cregger’s reboot of the video game property is set to decline around 60 percent to bring its North American sum to $103.6 million.
Robert Pattinson stars as journalist Chris Hansen in A24’s Primetime , which collected around $8.4 million on Friday, including Thursday previews, to eye roughly $20.5 million from 2,800 North American theaters. Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo and Phoebe Bridgers also star in director Lance Oppenheim’s feature that has a $15 million production budget and holds an 87 percent approval rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter , chief film critic David Rooney called it a “peak Sleaze TV rerun, for whoever wants it.”
Starring Brad Pitt as a Special Forces officer stranded with his combat dog in the wilderness, Paramount Pictures’ Heart of the Beast notched $7.4 million on Friday, including previews, and is expected to gross around $20 million domestically for the weekend from 3,400 North American locations. Carrying an $82 million production budget, director David Ayer’s movie stands at an 87 score from Rotten Tomatoes reviewers. THR critic Frank Scheck wrote that it “packs a surprising emotional punch.”
Rounding out the top five is DreamWorks Animation’s Forgotten Island , with the Universal Pictures release expected to scoop up around $11.5 million domestically for the weekend after bringing in $4.3 million on Friday, including Thursday previews and other advance screenings.
With a budget of $80 million, the film focuses on two friends magically transported to an island rooted in Philippine mythology. Featuring the voices of H.E.R., Liza Soberano and Dave Franco, Forgotten Island holds a 94 percent critic approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with Scheck writing for THR that it is “an exciting original.”
During the week, Universal Pictures became the first studio to surpass $5 billion at the 2026 global box office. The Odyssey , The Super Mario Galaxy Movie and Michael were among the hits helping Universal to reach this milestone for the first time since 2017.
Next weekend marks the opening for such high-profile releases as Warner Bros.’ Tom Cruise-led Digger and Amazon MGM Studios’ Verity , starring Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson.
